records.name: Prefix-free incompressibility characterization of Martin-Löf randomness
records.statement: For an infinite binary sequence X, X is Martin-Löf random iff there is a constant c such that for every n, K(X↾n) ≥ n-c.
hypotheses: X is an infinite binary sequence
K is prefix-free Kolmogorov complexity for a fixed optimal prefix-free machine

source_support.pointer: preprint p. 4; survey attributes the result to Schnorr/Levin

records.name: Basic strict hierarchy: Martin-Löf, computable, Schnorr randomness
records.statement: Martin-Löf randomness implies computable randomness, which implies Schnorr randomness, and neither implication reverses.
hypotheses: standard fair-coin Cantor-space versions of the notions in SRC-0007

source_support.pointer: Theorem 4.2 supplies high-degree witnesses for both non-reversals

records.name: Low for Martin-Löf randomness iff K-trivial
records.statement: A set A is low for Martin-Löf randomness iff A is K-trivial.
hypotheses: A is a set/real in the standard computability-theoretic setting

records.name: Bases for 1-randomness are exactly K-trivial sets
records.statement: A set B is a base for 1-randomness iff B is K-trivial.
hypotheses: base is in the sense of DEF-0009
1-randomness denotes Martin-Löf randomness in the source's context

records.name: Universal uniform randomness test on computable metric spaces
records.statement: Every computable metric space admits a universal uniform randomness test in the Hoyrup-Rojas framework.
hypotheses: space is a computable metric space
probability measures and tests use the representations/effectivity framework of SRC-0011

records.name: Schnorr randomness characterized by typicality for mixing computable dynamics
records.statement: In the computable-probability-space framework developed by Gács, Hoyrup and Rojas, a point is Schnorr random iff it is typical for every mixing computable dynamics.
hypotheses: computable probability space and the authors' effective dynamical notions

records.name: No-randomness-from-nothing separates computable from Schnorr randomness
records.statement: For almost-everywhere computable measure-preserving transformations on Cantor space, the no-randomness-from-nothing property holds for computable randomness but does not hold for Schnorr randomness.
hypotheses: F:2^N→2^N is almost-everywhere computable and measure-preserving, in the setting of SRC-0015

records.name: Martin-Löf randomness and the joint conservation/no-randomness-from-nothing property
records.statement: The results summarized in SRC-0015 imply that the Martin-Löf randoms form the largest subset of 2^N satisfying both no-randomness-from-nothing and randomness conservation for the almost-everywhere computable measure-preserving maps considered there.
hypotheses: Cantor-space setting and map class of SRC-0015
records.direction: maximality characterization stated in source abstract

records.name: Martin-Löf random sequences have constructive dimension 1
records.statement: Every Martin-Löf random infinite binary sequence has constructive dimension 1.
hypotheses: constructive dimension as developed in SRC-0013

records.name: Kolmogorov-complexity characterization of constructive dimension
records.statement: For an infinite binary sequence S, its constructive dimension is the limit inferior of the average prefix-free Kolmogorov complexity of its first n bits: dim(S)=liminf_n K(S↾n)/n.
hypotheses: constructive dimension and prefix-free K in the standard setting of the cited work

source_support.pointer: abstract explicitly attributes this theorem to Mayordomo

records.name: Dense Martin-Löf-random subsequences of KL-random sequences
records.statement: Every Kolmogorov-Loveland random sequence has arbitrarily dense subsequences that are Martin-Löf random.
hypotheses: KL-randomness and subsequence density as in SRC-0018

records.name: Total-Solovay characterization of Schnorr randomness
records.statement: A real y is Schnorr random iff y passes every total Solovay test, where a total Solovay test is a computable collection of c.e. open sets whose finite total measure sum is a computable real.
hypotheses: fair-coin/Lebesgue setting of SRC-0008
total Solovay test as DEF-0017

records.name: Computably graded-test characterization of computable randomness
records.statement: A real x is computably random iff it withstands every computably graded test; SRC-0024 also gives effective transformations from a computable martingale to such a test and conversely.
hypotheses: x∈2^ω
computable martingales and computably graded tests are as in SRC-0024 Definitions 2 and 5

records.name: High-degree witnesses separate Martin-Löf, recursive/computable and Schnorr randomness
records.statement: For every set A, A is high iff its Turing degree contains a recursively random but non-Martin-Löf-random set, equivalently iff it contains a Schnorr-random but non-recursively-random set; the same equivalence holds when the witnesses are required to be left-r.e.
hypotheses: standard fair-coin notions in SRC-0028
'recursively random' is the computable-martingale notion DEF-0004

records.name: c.e. Schnorr-random non-Martin-Löf-random separation witness
records.statement: There exists a computably enumerable real that is Schnorr random but not Martin-Löf random.
hypotheses: real in the setting of SRC-0008

records.name: Schnorr randomness strictly implies Kurtz randomness
records.statement: In Wang's notation S-RAND is a proper subset of W-RAND: every Schnorr-random sequence is Kurtz random, and there is a Kurtz-random sequence that is not Schnorr random.
hypotheses: fair-coin infinite-sequence notions in SRC-0029
S-RAND denotes Schnorr randomness; W-RAND denotes Kurtz randomness

records.name: Strict weak-n / n-random sandwich
records.statement: For every n≥1, weak (n+1)-randomness implies n-randomness, and n-randomness implies weak n-randomness; neither converse holds.
hypotheses: weak n-randomness as DEF-0014
n-randomness means the usual n-th Martin-Löf-relative level in SRC-0027
records.direction: two strict implications for each n≥1

records.name: Generalized Martin-Löf-test characterization of weak 2-randomness
records.statement: A real is weakly 2-random iff it passes every generalized Martin-Löf test.
hypotheses: generalized Martin-Löf test as DEF-0016
fair-coin Cantor-space setting

records.name: Kurtz randomness has equivalent weak test and martingale formulations
records.statement: Wang proves W-RAND = MW-RAND = SW-RAND = So-W-RAND. In particular, the weak/Kurtz class can be characterized by the sw-tests of Definition 3.1.25, which use a recursive martingale F and a recursive unbounded nondecreasing threshold h.
hypotheses: definitions 3.1.23-3.1.26 of SRC-0029
fair-coin sequence space

records.name: Martingale resource formulations distinguish Martin-Löf, computable and Schnorr randomness
records.statement: In SRC-0028's martingale formulation: Martin-Löf randomness forbids success by any r.e. martingale; recursive/computable randomness forbids success by any recursive martingale; Schnorr randomness forbids a recursive martingale M together with a recursive nondecreasing unbounded rate r for which M(X↾n)>r(n) infinitely often.
hypotheses: subset of N identified with its binary characteristic sequence
martingale success means unbounded limsup capital
